verdict.reasoning: Patient states, "I just noticed this like about a week ago" and confirms "it's the, the left elbow," indicating left elbow swelling for about a week.
Patient says, "It's not painful at all," describes it as "slightly warm," and "I, I, cannot feel like this, little bit fluid in inside," supporting non-painful, slightly warm, fluid-filled swelling.
On trauma: Doctor asks, "have you banged that elbow?" and patient replies, "No, not really. Um, not that I know of." On range of motion: patient says, "I can actually like move it normally."
When asked if this happened before, patient states, "No, no I haven't noticed that before... I don't have any like history of, of seeing this."
Patient says, "I think I have something like uh, osteoarthritis" and later confirms to the doctor, "Um, yes. Yes, a few years ago" when asked if a doctor has told him he has osteoarthritis.
Doctor asks, "are you on any medication on a regular basis?" and patient answers, "Uh, no."
Patient states, "I'm, I'm allergic to, to peanuts."
Doctor asks, "are, are you allergic to any medication?" and patient replies, "Uh, no. Not that I know of."
Doctor asks about family rheumatologic diseases; patient says, "in my family, I'm not sure... No," which amounts to denying known family history of rheumatoid arthritis or lupus.
Job: patient says, "No, I just, you know sit at a desk." Activity: "I do some sports. I run regularly, like two, three times a week... I'm, think I'm healthy," matching a fit, active lifestyle.

Video exam: doctor visually inspects elbow via camera. Warmth: doctor asks, "is it hot, compared to the surrounding skin?" and patient replies, "It's a bit warm, yes." Left side confirmed earlier as "the, the left elbow."

Patient reports, "On the tip of the elbow, it's, it's OK, just like, next to it like where the, the swelling is, it's a bit, yeah it feels weird," supporting non-tender tip with adjacent area feeling "weird."
Patient states, "I can actually like move it normally," indicating preserved/full range of motion.
Doctor notes on exam, "I noticed the skin was a bit dry, , on the tip of the elbow."

Doctor says, "this seems like uh, what we call the Bursitis" of the elbow. History includes one-week atraumatic swelling with warmth, minimal discomfort and normal movement. Doctor also states, "It doesn't look like, to me that's something called... septic arthritis" and "your joint doesn't look like that," showing low concern for septic arthritis.
Doctor advises, "I would take Ibuprofen regularly... that's four hundred milligrams, two times a day. And you should take that after food... If you get any heartburn, stop taking it."

Doctor plans blood tests: "having some tests done to check for inflammatory markers, infection, rheumatological antibodies... and also check for things like Gout as well." Timing: "results will come back to us after about five or six days."

Doctor says, "we can arrange a follow-up appointment for you, in one of our clinics" and later, "the follow-up appointment doesn't have to be face-to-face... we can do that over the phone, uh, over video... that's your call. But you contact us, after you've had the blood test done, and we can review things then."

Doctor advises, "if your, the elbow was to become very red, very painful, uh, and the redness was to spread or become uh, you know more intense. Then you need to get on the phone or get... a video appointment... as soon as possible. 'Cause that would be an emergency." Also notes current low concern for septic arthritis: "your joint doesn't look like that" and "this is not the case right now."

Doctor reassures: "No. I, I don't think this is anything dangerous. don't need to worry... Right now, it looks quite straightforward. It's nothing sinister or life-threatening," clearly providing reassurance.
